papers.title_in_file: Direct Generation and Detection of Correlated Photons with 3.2 um Wavelength Spacing
papers.version_note: arXiv:1708.05909v2, 13 Sep 2017; text matches the record.
papers.what_it_is: An experimental paper reporting SPDC pairs at 779.8 nm and 3950 nm in a PPLN waveguide, with the idler detected by upconversion to 651.2 nm and a Si-APD, and a coincidence-to-accidental ratio of 54.

assertions.value: The authors state that the SPDC process converts a 651.2 nm pump photon into a 779.8 nm signal photon and a 3950 nm idler photon.
quotes: For the current SPDC process where a 651.2 nm pump photon downconverts to a pair of a 779.8 nm signal photon and a 3950 nm idler photon.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 1 states the process wavelengths as the paper's own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that the pair detuning is over 3.2 microns, or more than 300 THz, and claim it is the largest detuning thus far in any waveguide-based photon source.
quotes: The detuning of the pair is over 3.2 microns, or >300 THz, which is the largest detuning thus far in any waveguide-based photon source.
assertions.certainty_reason: A priority claim by the authors, with no survey in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that prior correlated-photon techniques have been developed only in the visible and near-IR spectra, and that photon pairs were generated at 3.1 microns only very recently, with similar wavelengths and rather limited correlation (attributed to other work).
quotes: but only in the visible and near-IR spectra
Only very recently, photon pairs have been generated at 3.1 microns, albeit with similar wavelengths and rather limited
assertions.certainty_reason: A literature statement attributed to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that the waveguide has a silicon-dioxide cladded core with 3.5 um height and 11 um top width ridge structure, designed so that all lightwaves are in their respective fundamental quasi-TM modes for maximum overlap, and that FEM simulation of the actual waveguide parameters indicates a good mode overlap.
quotes: a silicon-dioxide cladded core with 3.5 um height (D) and 11 um top width (Wt) ridge structure
so that all lightwaves are in their respective fundamental quasi-transverse-magnetic (quasi-TM) modes for the maximum overlap
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 1 states the device geometry as the paper's own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that the waveguide is periodically poled with a domain length of 16.7 micron for quasi-phase matching, and that its temperature is stabilized at 32.2 ± 0.1 °C.
quotes: the waveguide is periodically poled with a domain length of 16.7 micron
stabilized at 32.2 ± 0.1 ◦C
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 1 states the poling and temperature as the paper's own setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that a 651.2 nm pulse train with 10 MHz repetition rate and 130 ps pulse width is coupled into a 2.2-cm long PPLN waveguide for SPDC.
quotes: A 651.2 nm pulse train with 10 MHz repetition rate and 130 ps pulse width is coupled
into a 2.2-cm long PPLN waveguide
assertions.certainty_reason: The Figure 2 caption states the pump and waveguide as setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that the signal photons pass a filter set of 3 nm bandwidth and are detected by a free-running fiber-coupled Si-APD (ID100) with 12.5 % quantum efficiency and dark-count rate below 1.4 Hz.
quotes: bandwidth: 3 nm; extinction: 140 dB
12.5 % quantum efﬁciency and low dark-count rate (<1.4 Hz)
assertions.certainty_reason: Figure 2 caption and Methods state the signal detector as setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that idler photons are upconverted by 779.8 nm pump pulses (779.8 nm + 3950 nm -> 651.2 nm) in a second PPLN waveguide with temperature stabilized at 62.2 ± 0.1 °C, and the 651.2 nm light is detected by a second Si-APD.
quotes: temperature stabilized at 62.2 ± 0.1 ◦C for the optimum phase matching
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the upconversion setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that the upconverted idler photons are detected by a free-running Si-APD (ID100) with 22.5% quantum efficiency and dark count below 1.8 Hz, behind an infrared narrow band filter with 60 nm FWHM in the Methods; the caption of the setup figure gives 90 nm for the same filter.
quotes: FWHM bandwidth: 60 nm
bandwidth: 90 nm; extinction: 70 dB
22.5% quantum efﬁciency and low dark count (< 1.8 Hz)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper gives two different filter bandwidths, so the setup value is not settled.
assertions.reader_inference: The Figure 2 caption (90 nm) and Methods (60 nm) disagree on the 3950 nm filter bandwidth; the Section 2 text also uses 22% for the same detector.

assertions.value: The authors report that the Si-APD has 50 ps timing resolution and the TDC has 66 ps root-mean-square timing resolution and 27 ps time-bin resolution.
quotes: The Si-APD has 50 ps timing resolution while the TDC has 66 ps root-mean-square timing resolution and 27 ps time-bin resolution.
assertions.certainty_reason: Methods states the timing hardware as setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that the signal-photon generation probability depends linearly on pump peak power, and that from the slope the SPDC efficiency is estimated to be -87 dB, about one in every 5 × 108 pump photons (exponent printed flat; read as ten to the eighth) downconverting into a correlated pair.
quotes: which displays a linear dependence, as expected
From the slope, the SPDC efﬁciency is estimated to be -87 dB
about one in every 5 × 108 pump photons
assertions.certainty_reason: One measurement from a single device.

assertions.value: The authors report a single-photon pulse of 130 ps FWHM after the filters, an effective spectral bandwidth of 3 nm FWHM, and effectively 100 detected time-frequency modes at 780 nm.
quotes: shown a single-photon pulse of 130 ps full width at half maximum (FWHM) after the ﬁlters
The cascaded ﬁlters centered at 780 nm provide an effective spectral bandwidth of 3 nm (FWHM)
so that there are effectively 100 detected time-frequency modes
assertions.certainty_reason: One measurement; the mode count is the authors' estimate.
assertions.reader_inference: Section 2 later uses 144 detected modes for the upconverted side; the 100 here is for the 780 nm side.

assertions.value: The paper states, citing other work, that superconducting nanowire detectors cover visible to mid-IR in principle but show a sharp decline in detection efficiency with a rapid rise of intrinsic dark count in the mid-IR regime.
quotes: there is a sharp decline in the detection efﬁciency accompanied by a rapid rise of intrinsic dark count in the mid-IR regime
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work.

assertions.value: The authors report that the phase matching bandwidth of the upconversion waveguide is measured to be 5.6 nm FWHM, corresponding to 107 GHz.
quotes: The phase matching bandwidth of the waveguide is measured to be 5.6 nm (FWHM), corresponding to 107 GHz in spectral bandwidth.
assertions.certainty_reason: One measurement.
assertions.reader_inference: Delta nu = c Delta lambda / lambda^2 at 3950 nm gives about 108 GHz, consistent with the stated 107 GHz.

assertions.value: The authors report a highest internal conversion efficiency of 33.9 ± 1.8% at an upconversion pump peak power of 3.8 W, with the efficiency decreasing as power rises further, which they attribute likely to multiple spatial modes.
quotes: with the highest conversion efﬁciency 33.9 ± 1.8% achieved at the peak pump power of 3.8 W
The efﬁciency decreases as the power further increases.
This saturation of conversion efﬁciency is likely due to the existence of multiple spatial modes for the photons.
assertions.certainty_reason: One measurement on one device; the saturation cause is the authors' suggestion.
assertions.reader_inference: The efficiency is inferred from signal counts and independently characterized losses, not measured directly (Methods p.21).

assertions.value: The authors state that the internal conversion efficiency is derived by dividing the true upconverted idler counts (SPDC on minus SPDC off) by the correlated signal counts, after correcting for linear losses and Si-APD quantum efficiencies, with a measured loss of about 16 dB from SPDC output to upconversion waveguide output (about 3 dB mirror output coupling, 1 dB filters and dichroic, 12 dB input coupling and propagation).
quotes: the internal upconversion efﬁciency was characterized by dividing the true upconverted idler-photon counts by the correlated signal-photon counts
is measured to be about 16 dB by using a weak coherent light at 3950 nm
About 3 dB loss is caused by the output coupling loss of the off-axis parabolic mirror, 1 dB of loss is from the 3950 nm bandpass ﬁlters and dichroic beam splitters
another 12 dB is from the input coupling efﬁciency and propagation loss of the upconversion waveguide
assertions.certainty_reason: Methods defines how the internal efficiency is obtained.
assertions.reader_inference: Methods also gives 19 dB total transmission before the Si-APD and about 4 dB afterward; 16 + 4 = 20 dB differs from 19 dB, presumably rounding.

assertions.value: The authors report that modal decomposition of the joint spectral function finds about 15 SPDC modes, approximately BT/4, and that a coupled-equation simulation with no free fitting parameter agrees well with the measured conversion efficiency, with slight discrepancy attributed to neglected higher-order pump modes and propagation loss.
quotes: This calculation ﬁnds a total number of SPDC modes to be about 15, approximately equal to BT/4
which assumes no free ﬁtting parameter
It shows a good agreement with experimental results
assertions.certainty_reason: A single numerical simulation compared with one dataset.

assertions.value: The authors report that with 33.9% conversion efficiency the noise photons are approximately 6.5×10−3 per pump pulse for 144 detected modes, and state this can be lowered to 4.5x10−5 per pulse if the number of detected modes is reduced to 1.
quotes: With a 33.9% conversion efﬁciency, the noise photons are approximately 6.5×10−3 per pump pulse for the 144 detected modes
4.5x10−5 per pulse if the number of the detected modes is reduced to 1
assertions.certainty_reason: One measurement; the 1-mode value is a projection.
assertions.reader_inference: Methods p.22 gives 3.8×10−4 per pulse for 144 modes at optimum efficiency and the abstract gives 2.6×10−6 per mode; 6.5×10−3/144 is 4.5×10−5, so the Section 2 figure is about 17 times the Methods figure. The paper does not reconcile them.

assertions.value: The authors report a noise detection of about 3.8×10−4 per pulse with 144 detection modes at optimum conversion efficiency, including detector dark count, upconversion noise and blackbody radiation, and the abstract gives 2.6×10−6 photon noise per time-frequency mode.
quotes: about 3.8×10−4 per pulse with 144 detection modes
2.6×10−6 photon noise per time-frequency mode
assertions.certainty_reason: One measurement.
assertions.reader_inference: 3.8×10−4/144 is 2.6×10−6, so the two statements agree with each other but not with Section 2's 6.5×10−3 per pulse.

assertions.value: The authors state that the majority of the noise counts come from spontaneous Raman scattering of the upconversion pump pulses falling in the filter window, that the noise count rate is higher with a wider bandpass filter, and that it depends linearly on pump peak power.
quotes: the majority of the dark counts are from the spontaneous Raman scattering of the upconversion pump pulses
the noise count rate is higher with wider bandpass ﬁlter
is linearly dependent on the pump peak power
assertions.certainty_reason: One measurement set with 144, 725 and 2900 modes.

assertions.value: The authors state that Raman scattering photons of the SPDC pump falling in the signal band are not expected to be significant because of the pump-signal detuning of more than 2500 cm−1.
quotes: is not expected to be signiﬁcant due to the large detuning between the pump and signal wavelength of more than 2500 cm−1
assertions.certainty_reason: An expectation stated without a measurement.

assertions.value: The authors state that the total detection efficiency of the 3950 nm photons is approximately 0.078% for the current under-optimized setup, and that it can be improved to 2.5% by shorter focal-length mirrors that cut waveguide coupling loss by 6 dB and Si-APDs with over 80% quantum efficiency.
quotes: the total detection efﬁciency of the 3950 nm single photons is approximately 0.078% for the current under-optimized setup
It can be improved signiﬁcantly to 2.5%
with over 80% quantum efﬁciency
reduce the total waveguide coupling loss by 6 dB
assertions.certainty_reason: The 0.078% is a derived figure for one setup; the 2.5% is a projection.

assertions.value: The authors define a coincident detection as both Si-APDs clicking within the coincidence window and an accidental coincidence as both clicking outside it, and obtain true coincidences by subtracting accidental from total coincidences.
quotes: A coincident detection is registered when both Si-APD
an accidentalcoincidence detection is recorded when both Si-APDs click outside the coincidence window
are obtained by subtracting the accidental coincidence from the total coincidence
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 3 defines the quantities.

assertions.value: The authors report that the true coincidence depends linearly on SPDC pump power and the accidental coincidence depends quadratically on it.
quotes: the true coincidence is linearly dependent on the pump power, as expected for SPDC
depends quadratically on the pump peak power
assertions.certainty_reason: One measurement set.

assertions.value: The authors report a maximum coincidence-to-accidental ratio (CAR) of 54±7 at a peak power of 9.7 mW, with a true coincidence count of 275 within an integration time of 300 s, limited by uncorrelated noise photons and dark counts of the upconversion detection system.
quotes: A maximum CAR of 54±7 is obtained at a peak power of 9.7 mW
limited by the uncorrelated noise photons and dark counts of the upconversion detection system
we obtained a true coincidence count of 275 within an integration time of 300 s
assertions.certainty_reason: A single-study empirical result.

assertions.value: The authors report that at lower pump power the CAR is only around 10 to 20, which they attribute to low pair-generation rate relative to the total dark count rate, and that at high pump power multiphoton effects raise accidental coincidences and lower the CAR.
quotes: For lower pump power, the CAR is only around 10∼20
the multiphoton effect involving the simultaneous generation of more than a photon pair increases the probability of accidental-coincidence detection
assertions.certainty_reason: One measurement set; the attributions are the authors' explanation.

assertions.value: The authors report, from total detection efficiencies of 1.3% (signal) and 0.078% (idler), a photon pair production rate of about 9.4 × 104 pair per second (exponent printed flat; read as ten to the fourth) and a spectral brightness of 4.4 × 102 pair/s/nm/mW (ten squared), and expect two orders of magnitude improvement with GHz-repetition-rate pump pulses.
quotes: Considering the total detection efﬁciency of 1.3% and 0.078% for the signal and idler
the photon pair production rate is about 9.4 × 104 pair per second
spectral brightness of 4.4 × 102 pair/s/nm/mW
assertions.certainty_reason: A derived figure for one setup; the improvement is a projection.

assertions.value: The authors state that a CAR of 54 gives a Franson visibility of 96% for time-energy entanglement, on par with existing SPDC sources in common wavelengths,.
quotes: With CAR of 54±7, this SPDC source can already be used
This gives a Franson visibility of 96% in the context of time-energy entanglement
on par with existing SPDC sources in visible and near-IR
assertions.certainty_reason: Computed from the CAR by the authors, not measured.
assertions.reader_inference: No Franson interferometer measurement is described; the 96% follows from the CAR formula (53/55) and assumes the CAR reflects pair purity.

assertions.value: The authors state that by detecting the signal photons the 3950 nm idler photons can be heralded, with a second-order correlation g2(0) = 0.08 ± 0.015.
quotes: the generation of idlers photons at 3950 nm can be heralded, with a second-order correlation g2(0) = 0.08 ± 0.015
assertions.certainty_reason: No g2(0) measurement is described in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper describes no heralded g2 measurement; the value appears to be derived from the CAR.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that they demonstrated direct generation and detection of high-purity photon pairs across 780 nm and 3950 nm using only room-temperature optics.
quotes: We have demonstrated direct generation and detection of high-purity photon pairs across the visible/near-IR (780 nm) and mid-IR (3950 nm) spectra, using only room-temperature optics.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' conclusion.
assertions.reader_inference: Purity is inferred from the CAR; no state tomography or interference is reported.

assertions.value: The authors claim the source can support heralded mid-IR single photons, free-space quantum communication in a transparent atmospheric window, and heralded or ghost imaging if a PPLN crystal replaces the waveguide.
assertions.anchor: Introduction p.3-4; Section 3 p.16; Section 4 p.18
quotes: mid-IR single photons can be generated via heralding
the 3950 nm photons are superior for free-space quantum communications
the same strong correlation of the photon pairs can be translated to the spatial
assertions.certainty_reason: Prospective applications, not demonstrated here.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum optical arbitrary waveform techniques could potentially improve the CAR by more than 20 times, to over 1000, while suppressing background noise further.
quotes: will potentially improve the coincidence-to-accidental coincidence ratio by >20 times (to over 1000)
assertions.certainty_reason: A projection, with no data in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state the current system is under-optimized: it is limited by waveguide coupling set by the off-axis parabolic mirror, by a number of detected time-frequency modes that raises noise, and by Si-APD quantum efficiency.
quotes: the coupling efﬁciency is mainly limited by the off-axis parabolic mirror
it is crucial to reduce it, in order to improve the signal-to-noise ratio
for the current under-optimized setup
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limitations.
